top_story: Netanyahu’s public rejection on 9 August of a US-backed 15-point Gaza plan, including any Israeli withdrawal before Hamas disarms, turns a private policy dispute into an open rupture with Washington and signals a continued military course despite external pressure. That stance lands against a much older baseline of extreme civilian devastation in Gaza, where prolonged war has made death, decomposition, and blocked recovery of the wounded and dead part of daily life rather than a temporary emergency. Two days earlier, Israel’s indictment of settler Yinon Levy over the killing of Palestinian activist Awdah Hathaleen in the occupied West Bank underscored how rare accountability remains even as settler violence sharpens Palestinian insecurity beyond Gaza. The combined picture is of an Israeli leadership resisting de-escalation while offering only narrow legal exceptions to broader coercive realities, leaving civilians across Palestinian territories exposed to deepening harm and little prospect of near-term relief.
